dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأثارة) With fatḥa on the hamza: a remnant of knowledge, an inherited noble trait, and a glorious deed; from their saying "the she-camel grew fat upon an athāra of fat", which is the remnant of it. From Ibn al-Aʿrābī: "so-and-so angered me upon an athāra of anger", i.e. on the trace of an anger that had been before that. And they have an athāra of knowledge, i.e. a remnant of it which they transmit (yaʾthurūnahā) from the ancients. One says: "the Banū so-and-so have an athāra of nobility" when they have ancient testimonies to it, and in other things. Al-Rāʿī said:
وذات أثارة أكلت علينا ... نباتا في أكمته قفارا
(And a she-camel with a remnant [of fat], which grazed, to our cost, on plants in its hillocks bare of all else.)
I.e. a remnant of fat. Al-Wāḥidī said: the speech of the lexicographers on this word revolves around three views. The first: al-athāra, derived from "athartu al-shayʾa uthīruhu athāratan", as though it were a remnant that is brought out and stirred up (tustathār). The second: from al-athar, which is narration (riwāya). The third: from al-athar in the sense of a sign.

* I'rab:
(حم تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ) (حم): the discussion of the openings of the surahs has already been given. (تنزيل الكتاب) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (من الله); and (العزيز الحكيم) are two naʿts (adjectives). (ما خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَما بَيْنَهُما إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى) (ما) is negating; (خلقنا السموات): a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (بالحق) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a creation bound up with the truth. The wāw is a conjunction; (أجل) is conjoined to (الحق), and (مسمى) is an adjective. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَمَّا أُنْذِرُوا مُعْرِضُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (عمّا) are attached to (معرضون); the clause (أنذروا) is a ṣila, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. "from what they were warned of"; and (معرضون) is the khabar of (الذين). It is also permissible for (ما) to be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. from their being warned of that Day. (قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَرُونِي ماذا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ) (قل) is an imperative verb with a latent (mustatir) agent; (أرأيتم) is a verb and its agent; (ما) is a direct object; the clause (تدعون) is the ṣila; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أروني) is an imperative verb with its agent and its object, and the clause is a tawkīd (emphasis) of (أرأيتم). The clause (ماذا خلقوا) is the second object of (أرأيتم); (ماذا) is a fronted object of (خلقوا); or (ما) is a mubtadaʾ and (ذا) a relative noun as its khabar, with the clause (خلقوا) as its ṣila. It is also permissible that (أروني) not be an emphasis of (أرأيتم), so that the matter belongs to the chapter of rivalry [of two governing words] (al-tanāzuʿ), because (أرأيتم) requires a second object and so does (أروني), and His words (ماذا خلقوا) are what they compete for. The text of Abū Ḥayyān's wording: «(قل أرأيتم ما تدعون) means: inform me about those whom you call upon besides Allah — and they are the idols. (أروني ماذا خلقوا من الأرض) is an interrogation of rebuke. The first object of (أرأيتم) is (ما تدعون), and (ماذا خلقوا) is an interrogative clause that (أرأيتم) requires, because its second object is an interrogative, and (أروني) requires it by way of suspension (taʿlīq). So this belongs to the chapter of governing (al-iʿmāl): the second was made to govern, and the second object of (أرأيتم) was omitted. It is possible that (أروني) is an emphasis of (أرأيتم) in the sense of "inform me", as though they have one meaning. Ibn ʿUqba said: (أرأيتم) admits two aspects: one, that it be transitive and (ما) its object; and it is possible that (أرأيتم) be a word of alerting, not transitive, with (ما) being interrogative in the sense of rebuke, and (تدعون) meaning "you worship".» [Translator's note: "Ibn ʿUqba" is as printed; Abū Ḥayyān here is likely quoting Ibn ʿAṭiyya.] End of quote. That (أرأيتم) is intransitive and a word of alerting is somewhat doubtful; al-Akhfash said it regarding His words (قال أرأيت إذ أوينا إلى الصخرة). What appears is that (ما تدعون) is the object of (أرأيتم), as in His words (قل أرأيتم شركاءكم الذين تدعون) in Sūrat Fāṭir, where the discussion of the counterpart of this clause has been given; and the discussion of (أرأيتم) was given in Sūrat al-Anʿām.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is as printed; the quotation from Abū Ḥayyān apparently continues to this point.] (من الأرض) is a ḥāl, because it explains the vague element in (ماذا خلقوا). (أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي السَّماواتِ ائْتُونِي بِكِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ هذا أَوْ أَثارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) (أم) is in the sense of the hamza of disapproval and the bal of digression (al-iḍrābiyya), so it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿa): it is as though He turned from the first interrogation to asking whether they have a share with Allah in the creation of the heavens and the earth, for shirk here means sharing. (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (شرك) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) are attached to (شرك). (ائتوني) is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object, and the clause is part of the completion of what is said; (بكتاب) are attached to (ائتوني); (من قبل هذا) is an adjective of (كتاب), i.e. existing from before this. (أو) is a conjunction; (أثارة) is conjoined to (بكتاب), and (من علم) is an adjective of (أثارة). (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then bring me [it]"; (صادقين) is the khabar of (كنتم). (وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَنْ لا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ) The wāw is resumptive; (من) is an interrogative noun whose meaning is disapproval, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (أضل) is the khabar; (ممّن) are attached to (أضل); the clause (يدعو) is the ṣila of (من); (من دون الله) is a ḥāl; (من) is the object of (يدعو), and the clause (لا يستجيب له) is the ṣila. They also permitted (من) to be a complete, described indefinite noun, so that the clause (لا يستجيب له) is an adjective. (إلى يوم القيامة) is a ḥāl. The meaning of the limit will come in the section on Rhetoric. (وَهُمْ عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ غافِلُونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عن دعائهم) are attached to (غافلون); (غافلون) is the khabar of (هم); and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words (إلى يوم القيامة) there is a splendid rhetorical subtlety: He made the Day of Resurrection the limit of their not responding, and it is in the nature of a limit that the meaning ends at it; yet the non-response continues after this limit, because on the Day of Resurrection too they will not respond to them. The right view is that it is one of those limits which indicate that what comes after them, even if it agrees with what precedes, exceeds it by a clear increase that attaches it to the second [state], so that the two states, though of one kind, are — because of the disparity between them — like a thing and its opposite. For the first state, whose limit is made the Resurrection, does not go beyond non-response, while the second state, on the Resurrection, adds to non-response enmity and the disowning of their worship of them. So it is of the same kind as what preceded in Sūrat al-Zukhruf in His words: (بل متّعت هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى جاءهم الحق ورسول مبين ولما جاء الحق قالوا: هذا سحر وإنّا به كافرون).
2- Predominance (al-taghlīb): the rational was given predominance over the non-rational, by way of going along [with them] (al-mujārāh), because the worshippers of idols used to describe them as having discernment, out of ignorance and stupidity.

dervis-irab:6-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِدْعاً) There are two views on it. One: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and so it involves the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being "one of novelty" (dhā bidʿ). The second: that bidʿ is itself an adjective on the pattern fiʿl in the sense of badīʿ (novel), like khiff and khafīf (light) and ḥibb and ḥabīb (beloved). The discussion of al-badīʿ has already been given at length, and that it is that whose like has never been seen, from al-ibtidāʿ, which is invention.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا حُشِرَ النَّاسُ كانُوا لَهُمْ أَعْداءً وَكانُوا بِعِبادَتِهِمْ كافِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (حشر الناس) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (الناس) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause (كانوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (كان) and its noun; (لهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and (أعداء) is the khabar (predicate) of (كانوا). (وكانوا) is conjoined to the first (وكانوا); (بعبادتهم) are attached to (كافرين); the hāʾ is annexed to (عبادة) as an annexation of the maṣdar to its object, i.e. "their being worshipped"; and (كافرين) is the khabar of (كانوا). (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ قالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا) is conjoined to what preceded; (بيّنات) is a ḥāl; and the clause (قال الذين كفروا) is the apodosis of (إذا), with no grammatical position. (للحق) are attached to (قالوا). The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «The lām in (للحق) is the lām of connection (lām al-ṣila), i.e. on account of the truth.» (لما) is temporal ("when") or linking; (جاءهم) is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent). (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (سحر) a khabar and (مبين) a naʿt (adjective); and the clause is the object of their saying. (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ قُلْ إِنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَلا تَمْلِكُونَ لِي مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً) (أم) is in the sense of bal and the hamza of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī): He turned from mentioning their calling it magic to mentioning their saying that Muḥammad fabricated it and wove its style of his own making — and that is more hideous than what came before, even though both spring from one source deeply sunk in error and disbelief. The clause (افتراه) is the object of their saying. (قل) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (إن) is conditional; (افتريته) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; (لا) is negating; (تملكون) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its agent; (لي) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تملكون); (من الله) is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective and was placed before what it describes; and (شيئا) is a direct object. (هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِما تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ) The clause is circumstantial; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (أعلم) a khabar; (بما) are attached to (أعلم), and the clause (تفيضون فيه) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (كَفى بِهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ) (كفى) is a past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun genitive in form, in the position of nominative as the agent; (شهيدا) is a tamyīz (specification); (بيني) is an adverb attached to (شهيدا), and (بينكم) an adverb conjoined to its like. The wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, and (الغفور الرحيم) are two khabars of it. (قُلْ ما كُنْتُ بِدْعاً مِنَ الرُّسُلِ وَما أَدْرِي ما يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلا بِكُمْ) (قل) is an imperative verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (ما) is negating; (كان) and its noun, and (بدعا) is its khabar; (من الرسل) is a naʿt of (بدعا). (ما) is conjoined to the first negating (ما); (أدري) is a nominative imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "we" [Translator's note: so in the source; the latent pronoun of (أدري) is "I" (أنا)]. (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يفعل), in the passive, is its khabar; it suspends (أدري) from governing, so it stands in place of its two objects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The (ما) in (ما يفعل) may be a relative noun in the accusative, or an interrogative in the nominative.» (بي) are attached to (يفعل), and (ولا بكم) is conjoined to it. (إِنْ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا ما يُوحى إِلَيَّ وَما أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) (إن) is negating; (أتبع) is a nominative imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "I"; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ما) is the object of (أتبع), and the clause (يوحى إليّ) is the ṣila. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (أنا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (نذير) is a khabar and (مبين) a naʿt.

dervis-irab:10-14.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ كانَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ) The clause (أرأيتم) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The two objects of (أرأيتم) are omitted, their implied form being "Have you considered your state if such-and-such were the case — are you not wrongdoers?" The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is also omitted, its implied form being "then you have done wrong". Al-Zamakhsharī supplied it as "are you not wrongdoers?", and Abū Ḥayyān rebutted him: were it so, the fāʾ would be obligatory, because when an interrogative clause occurs as the apodosis of a condition the fāʾ is required; then, if the interrogative particle is the hamza, it precedes the fāʾ, as in "if you visit us, do we then not honour you (a-fa-mā nukrimuka)?", and if it is something else, the fāʾ precedes it, as in "if you visit us, then do you see anything but good (fa-hal tarā)?". It was also said that the apodosis is (فآمن واستكبرتم); and it was said that it is omitted, its implied form being "then who among us is in the right and who is in the wrong?"; and it was said: "then who is further astray?". The noun of (كان) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it", and (من عند الله) is its khabar (predicate). (وكفرتم): the wāw is a conjunction and the clause (كفرتم) is conjoined to the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); al-Jalāl and al-Samīn chose that it be circumstantial. (به) are attached to (كفرتم). (وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (شهد شاهد) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من بني إسرائيل) is an adjective of (شاهد); (على مثله) are attached to (شهد). The pronoun refers back to the Quran, i.e. to the like of the Quran in the meanings found in the Torah that correspond to it — the affirmation of divine unity, the resurrection, the raising, and other matters. This likeness is in respect of the correspondence of meanings, even if the wordings differ. (فَآمَنَ وَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (آمن) is a verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "he", i.e. the witness; (استكبرتم) is conjoined to (فآمن). (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يهدي القوم الظالمين) is the khabar. (وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كانَ خَيْراً ما سَبَقُونا إِلَيْهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (قال الذين) is a verb and its agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (للذين) are attached to (قال), and the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila. (لو) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb whose noun is latent, referring to what Muḥammad brought; (خيرا) is its khabar. (ما) is negating; (سبقونا) is a verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إليه) are attached to (سبقونا). The [whole] clause is the object of the saying, and the clause (ما سبقونا إليه) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَإِذْ لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا بِهِ فَسَيَقُولُونَ هذا إِفْكٌ قَدِيمٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "their obstinacy became manifest", and His words (فسيقولون) are caused by it. (فسيقولون) does not govern (إذ) because the two times contradict each other, and also because of the fāʾ. It was also said: if there is no obstacle to (فسيقولون) governing the adverb except the incompatibility of indicating past and future, this is no obstacle, for the future here is only used to signal the continuation of what has occurred and passed; because the people were deprived of guidance and said "this is an ancient falsehood", "tales of the ancients", and so on. So the meaning of the verse is then: and they said, when they were not guided by it, "this is an ancient falsehood", and they continued in that and persisted in it; so its occurrence and then its continuation were expressed with the future form — just as Ibrāhīm said (إلا الذي فطرني فإنه سيهدين), when guidance had already occurred and passed, but he spoke of its occurrence and then its continuation and so expressed it with the future form; and this is the way to reconcile His words (سيهدين) with His words in the other [verse] (فهو يهدين). Were it not for the fāʾ entering the verb, what we have mentioned would be the right view; but the causative fāʾ, by entering, indicated an omitted element which is the cause, and cut the verb off from the preceding adverb, so it became necessary to supply the omitted element as what governs it.
Abū al-Suʿūd said in his tafsīr: «(وإذ لم يهتدوا به) is an adverb of an omitted element indicated by what precedes it and on which what follows it is consequent, i.e. and since they were not guided by the Quran they said what they said; (فسيقولون), not content with denying its goodness, (هذا إفك قديم), just as they said "tales of the ancients". It was said that the omitted element is "their obstinacy became manifest", but that is not quite it.» The wording of al-Karkhī: «His words (وإذ لم يهتدوا) are an adverb of an omitted element such as "their obstinacy became manifest", not of His words (فسيقولون), because that is for the future while (إذ) is for the past. It may also be said that (إذ) is causal, not adverbial; or it may be said that (فسيقولون) expresses continuity across the three times, with the sīn merely for emphasis. As for the fāʾ, it does not prevent governing what precedes it, as al-Raḍī and others stated explicitly; and the causation may be from their disbelief.»
(لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (يهتدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and the wāw is the agent. The fāʾ is a conjunction; the sīn is a particle of the future; (يقولون) is a nominative imperfect verb and its agent; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (إفك) a khabar and (قديم) an adjective; and the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying. (وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى إِماماً وَرَحْمَةً) The wāw is resumptive; (من قبله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (كتاب موسى) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and (إماما) and (رحمة) are two ḥāls (circumstantials) of (كتاب موسى). The implied form is: and the Book of Mūsā exists from before the Quran, in the state of being a guide and a mercy. (وَهذا كِتابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِساناً عَرَبِيًّا لِيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا وَبُشْرى لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ)
The wāw is a conjunction; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ, (كتاب) a khabar and (مصدّق) an adjective; (لسانا) is a ḥāl of the pronoun in (مصدّق) or of (كتاب), and what governs it is the meaning of the demonstrative. Abū al-Baqāʾ parsed it as a direct object of (مصدّق), in which case the reference is to something other than the Quran. It was also said that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in an Arabic tongue". Abū Ḥayyān permitted all these aspects. The lām is causal; (ينذر) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (مصدق); or it is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (الذين) is a direct object, and the clause (ظلموا) is the ṣila. (بشرى) is conjoined to the position of (لينذر) if it is an object of purpose; and it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and it is glad tidings"; (للمحسنين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (بشرى). (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا) (إن) and its noun; the clause (قالوا) is the ṣila; (ربنا) is a mubtadaʾ and (الله) a khabar, and the reverse is permissible; (ثم) is a conjunction, and the clause (استقاموا) is conjoined to the clause (قالوا). (فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of (إن), because of the scent of condition in the relative noun. Al-Samīn said: «The fāʾ is redundant in the khabar of the relative noun because of the sense of condition in it; and (إن) did not prevent that, because the meaning of al-intidāb remains [Translator's note: so in the print; probably a misprint for al-ibtidāʾ, "the subject–predicate relation"], unlike laʿalla, layta and kaʾanna.» Sībawayh holds that (إن) is supposed to be removed, and then the fāʾ entered the khabar of (الذين). (لا) is negating; (خوف) is a mubtadaʾ, allowed to begin the sentence [though indefinite] because the negation precedes it; and (عليهم) is the khabar. (ولا هم يحزنون) is conjoined to the preceding clause, and the clause (فلا خوف عليهم) is the khabar of (إن). (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ خالِدِينَ فِيها جَزاءً بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب الجنة) its khabar; (خالدين فيها) is a ḥāl; (جزاء) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "they are recompensed with a recompense", and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted parsing it as a ḥāl. (بما) are attached to (جزاء); (ما) is a relative noun or maṣdariyya; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يعملون) is its khabar; and the clause [أولئك أصحاب الجنة] is a second khabar of (إن).

dervis-irab:15-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَفِصالُهُ) In al-Mukhtār: «al-fiṣāl is weaning (al-fiṭām).» It was also read (وفصله); faṣl and fiṣāl are like ʿaẓm and ʿiẓām in form and meaning [Translator's note: so in the source]. What is meant by it will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ) The explanation of al-ashudd has been given before. The wording of al-Kashshāf: «Reaching al-ashudd is that he enters mature age and completes the age at which his strength, intellect and discernment become firm, and that is when he passes thirty and approaches forty.»
(أَوْزِعْنِي) Inspire me; its explanation has been given before.

* I'rab:
(وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ إِحْساناً) Resumptive speech, introduced to show the lesson in the varying state of a person with his parents: he may obey them and he may oppose them; and as long as a person is grounded in this disposition, the like of this with the Prophet ﷺ is not far-fetched. (وصينا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الإنسان) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بوالديه) are attached to (وصّينا); and (إحسانا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) made accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. We enjoined him to do good to them with a doing of good. It was also said that it is a direct object, with (وصينا) carrying the meaning of "We made binding", so that it is a second object; and it was said rather that it is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. We enjoined him concerning them out of beneficence from Us towards them. It was also read (حسنا), and its i'rab is as above. (حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهاً وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهاً) The clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for the injunction mentioned. (حملته أمه): a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. (كرها), with ḍamma or fatḥa on the kāf — it has been read with both — is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent, i.e. "in a state of hardship"; it may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a hard carrying". (ووضعته كرها) is conjoined to what preceded. (وَحَمْلُهُ وَفِصالُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْراً) The wāw is of ḥāl; (حمله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (فصاله) is conjoined to (حمله); (ثلاثون) is the khabar (predicate) and (شهرا) a tamyīz (specification). (حَتَّى إِذا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً) (حتى) is a particle of limit and of the genitive, i.e. and he lived until he reached his full strength. (إذا) is an adverb of future time; the clause (بلغ أشده) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (بلغ) is conjoined to the first (بلغ); (أربعين) is a direct object and (سنة) a tamyīz; and a muḍāf must be supplied, i.e. "the completion of forty". (قالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلى والِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صالِحاً تَرْضاهُ) The clause (قال) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (رب) is a munādā (one addressed) annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, as has been established before. (أوزعني) is an imperative verb used for supplication; (أن) and what is in its domain are in the position of accusative as the object of (أوزعني); (نعمتك) is the object of (أشكر); (التي) is an adjective of (نعمتك), and the clause (أنعمت عليّ) is the ṣila (relative clause). (وأن أعمل) is conjoined to (أن أشكر); (صالحا) is a direct object or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar; and the clause (ترضاه) is an adjective of "a deed" (ʿamalan). (وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي إِنِّي تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) (وأصلح) is conjoined to (أوزعني); (لي) are attached to (أصلح); (في ذريتي) are attached to an omitted ḥāl. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: what is the meaning of (وأصلح لي في ذريتي)? I say: its meaning is that He make his offspring a place for righteousness and a likely seat of it, as though he said: grant me righteousness in my offspring and make it occur in them.» Better than that is the wording of al-Shihāb al-Khafājī in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī: «That is, the apparent form would have been "make righteous for me my offspring", because iṣlāḥ is transitive, as in His words, Exalted is He, (وأصلحنا له زوجه). So it was said that it was made transitive with fī because it carries the meaning of being gracious, i.e. be gracious to me in my offspring; or it was treated as intransitive and then made transitive with fī to convey the pervasion of righteousness in them and their being like a vessel for it, because of its firmness in them; and this is what the author intended, and it is the best.» (إن) and its noun, and the clause (تبت) is its khabar; (إليك) are attached to (تبت); and (إني من المسلمين) is conjoined to (إني تبت إليك). (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ ما عَمِلُوا) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذين) its khabar; the clause (نتقبل عنهم) is the ṣila; (أحسن) is a direct object; (ما) is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila. (ما) may also be maṣdariyya, i.e. "the best of their deeds". (وَنَتَجاوَزُ عَنْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ فِي أَصْحابِ الْجَنَّةِ وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ) (ونتجاوز) is conjoined to (نتقبل), falling within the domain of the ṣila; (عن سيئاتهم) are attached to (نتجاوز); and (في أصحاب الجنة) is a ḥāl. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «If you say: what is the meaning of His words (في أصحاب الجنة)? I say: it is like your saying "the emir honoured me among people of his companions", meaning he honoured me among the whole of those he honoured of them and placed me in their number. Its position is accusative as a ḥāl, in the sense of "being among the people of the Garden and counted among them".» Abū al-Baqāʾ and others permitted the preposition and its genitive noun to be in the position of nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are among the people of the Garden". (وعد الصدق) is a maṣdar made accusative by its implied verb, i.e. Allah promised them the promise of truth, i.e. a truthful promise; it is a maṣdar emphasising the content of the preceding clause. (الذي) is an adjective of (وعد الصدق); the clause (كانوا يوعدون) is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the clause (يوعدون) is the khabar of (كانوا). (يوعدون) is a passive nominative imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَالَّذِي قالَ لِوالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُما) (والذي) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar will come later; the clause (قال) is the ṣila; (لوالديه) are attached to (قال). (أفّ) is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, meaning "I am vexed"; the discussion of it has been given before. (لكما)
is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, because the lām is for clarification (li-l-bayān). (أَتَعِدانِنِي أَنْ أُخْرَجَ وَقَدْ خَلَتِ الْقُرُونُ مِنْ قَبْلِي) The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (تعدانني) is a nominative imperfect verb, its agent and its direct object; (أن أخرج) is interpreted as a maṣdar, a second object of (تعدانني), or accusative by removal of the preposition; (أخرج) is a passive imperfect verb. (وقد): the wāw is of ḥāl and (قد) is a particle of realisation; (خلت القرون) is a verb and its agent; (من قبلي) are attached to (خلت). (وَهُما يَسْتَغِيثانِ اللَّهَ وَيْلَكَ آمِنْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ فَيَقُولُ ما هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (هما) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يستغيثان) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and the Name of Majesty is a direct object. Istaghātha is transitive sometimes by itself and at other times with the bāʾ, but in the Quran it occurs only as transitive by itself. Al-Rāzī said: «Its meaning is: they seek help from Allah against his disbelief; when the preposition was dropped, the verb reached [the object] directly. It was also said: istighātha is supplication, so there is no need for the bāʾ.» (ويلك) is a maṣdar whose verb the Arabs have let die out, and the clause is governed by an implied saying, i.e. they say "woe to you, believe!"; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. they seek Allah's help, saying… The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: «(ويلك) is a maṣdar whose verb is not used; and it was said that it is a direct object, i.e. may Allah make your woe binding on you.» (آمن) is an imperative verb from īmān, and it is part of what they say. (إن) with its noun and khabar, and the clause gives the reason for the command and has no grammatical position. The fāʾ is conjoined to the omitted saying; (ما) is negating; (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أساطير الأولين) is the khabar of (هذا); and the clause is the object of the saying.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا» there is a synecdochic trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is adjacency, because al-fiṣāl is weaning, and what is meant by it here is its period, which weaning follows.

* Benefits:
1- These verses contain unique teachings on dutifulness to parents, because honouring them is among the deeds that Allah the Exalted loves, and it equals the reward of striving in His path. No wonder, for Allah has joined His good pleasure to theirs. This has already been mentioned in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, where He, Exalted is He, says: «واعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وبالوالدين إحسانا»; and He, Exalted is He, said in Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt: «ووصّينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إليّ مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون». Muslim narrated by way of Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd from his father, who said: Umm Saʿd swore that she would never speak to him until he disbelieved in his religion. She said: "You claim that Allah has enjoined you concerning your parents; I am your mother and I command you to do this." Then the verse was revealed. And from Abū Bakra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Shall I not tell you of the greatest of the major sins?" — three times. We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to parents." He had been reclining, and he sat up and said: "And beware of false speech and false testimony", and he kept repeating it until we said: "Would that he would stop." Narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. The meaning is: we wished he would stop out of concern for him, because of the signs of his agitation over that which they saw. Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd said: his concern ﷺ with false testimony may be because it occurs more easily among people, they are more careless about it, and its harm occurs more often; for a Muslim recoils from shirk and one's nature recoils from disobedience to parents, but as for false speech, the motives for it are many, so it was fitting to give it attention — and that is not because of its gravity relative to what was mentioned with it.
2- The period of pregnancy: Abū Ḥayyān said: (وحمله وفصاله ثلاثون شهرا), i.e. the period of his carrying and his weaning. This can only be if one of the two ends is reduced: either the woman gives birth at six months and suckles for two years, or she gives birth at nine months, as is customary, and suckles for two years less a quarter of a year. If the period of pregnancy increases, the period of suckling decreases, so the period of suckling is a year and nine months, and completing the two years is for whoever wishes to complete the suckling. Experience has shown that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, as the Quran states. Galen said: I investigated the length of pregnancy intensively, and I saw a woman who gave birth after one hundred and eighty-four nights; and Ibn Sīnā claimed that he witnessed that. As for the maximum period of pregnancy, there is nothing in the Quran indicating it. It is related that Aristotle said: the period of gestation of every animal is fixed except for man; she may give birth at seven months or at eight, and the child seldom survives in the eighth except in certain lands such as Egypt.
3- A subtle point: He, Exalted is He, mentioned the mother in three degrees — in His words (بوالديه), in her carrying him, and in her suckling him, expressed by weaning — and mentioned the father in one, in His words (بوالديه). This accords with what the Messenger said, assigning three quarters of dutifulness to the mother and a quarter to the father, when a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, to whom should I be dutiful?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then whom?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then whom?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "Then whom?" He said: "Your father."

dervis-irab:18-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأحقاف) He said in al-Qāmūs: «al-ḥiqf, with kasra, is a curved stretch of sand; the plural is aḥqāf, ḥiqāf and ḥuqūf, and the plural of the plural is ḥaqāʾif and ḥiqafa; or it is a great round sand-hill, or an elongated overlooking one; or they are elongated sands in the region of al-Shiḥr.» Its commentator said in al-Tāj: «And by it His words, Exalted is He, were explained: "And mention the brother of ʿĀd, when he warned his people at al-Aḥqāf". Al-Jawharī said: and it is the land of ʿĀd. Ibn ʿArafa said: the people of ʿĀd had their dwellings among the sands, and those are al-Aḥqāf. In al-Muʿjam: it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that it is a valley between ʿUmān and the land of Mahra. Ibn Isḥāq said: al-Aḥqāf is sand between ʿUmān and Ḥaḍramawt. Qatāda said: al-Aḥqāf are sands overlooking Hajar in al-Shiḥr, in the land of Yemen. Yāqūt said: so these are three views that do not differ in meaning.» Also in al-Qāmūs: «al-shajr, like al-manʿ, is opening the mouth; and the seacoast between ʿUmān and ʿAdan; and it may be pronounced with kasra.» [Translator's note: so printed (al-shajr, with jīm); the place-name under discussion is al-Shiḥr, with ḥāʾ.] Abū Ḥayyān said: «al-ḥiqf is an elongated, raised stretch of sand with curvature and bending in it; from it comes iḥqawqafa al-shayʾ, the thing became curved. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فلما أجزنا ساحة الحيّ وانتحى ... بنا بطن خبت ذي حقاف عقنقل
(When we had crossed the tribe's open ground and the hollow of a low plain with winding, piled-up sand-dunes turned aside with us.)»
His commentator al-Zawzanī said: «al-ḥiqf is overlooking, curved sand; the plural is aḥqāf and ḥiqāf.» The wording of al-Kashshāf: «al-Aḥqāf is the plural of ḥiqf, which is elongated raised sand with a bend in it, from iḥqawqafa al-shayʾ when it became curved. ʿĀd were people of pillars, dwelling among sands overlooking the sea in a land called al-Shiḥr, in the country of Yemen; and it was said: between ʿUmān and Mahra.» Ibn Zayd said: «They are sands overlooking the sea, elongated like mountains, but not reaching the point of being mountains.» Muqātil said: the dwellings of ʿĀd were in Yemen, in Ḥaḍramawt, at a place called Mahra, to which the Mahrī camels are attributed. Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī] said, satirising Kāfūr:
ويلمّها خطة ويلم قابلها ... لمثلها خلق المهرية القود
(Woe to such a plan, and woe to the one who accepts it — for the like of it the long-necked Mahrī camels were created [i.e. to flee from it].)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said in his commentary on the Dīwān: al-mahriyya: attributed to Mahra ibn Ḥaydān, a clan of Quḍāʿa.
(عارِضاً) Al-ʿāriḍ: the cloud that spreads across the horizon of the sky. Abū Ḥayyān said: al-ʿāriḍ is the rain-bearing cloud that stretches across the sky; from it is the poet's saying:
يا من رأى عارضا أرقت له ... بين ذراعي وجبهة الأسد
(O you who saw a spreading cloud for which I stayed awake, between the two forearms and the forehead of the Lion [constellation].)
Al-Aʿshā said:
يا من رأى عارضا قد بتّ أرمقه ... كأنه البرق في حافاته الشعل
(O you who saw a spreading cloud that I spent the night watching, as though the lightning on its edges were flames.)

* I'rab:
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلُ فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذين) its khabar (predicate); the clause (حق عليهم القول) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (في أمم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the noun made genitive by (على); the clause (قد خلت) is an adjective of (أمم); (من قبلهم) are attached to (خلت); and (من الجن) is a second adjective of (أمم). (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا خاسِرِينَ) (إن) and its noun, and the clause (كانوا) is its khabar; (خاسرين) is the khabar of (كانوا); and the clause has no grammatical position because it gives a reason. (وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجاتٌ مِمَّا عَمِلُوا وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أَعْمالَهُمْ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (لكل) is a fronted khabar and (درجات) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (مما) is an adjective of (درجات), and the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila. (وليوفّيهم):
the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal; (يوفّيهم) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted thing that is given a cause, as though it were said "and He recompensed them with that in order to pay them in full". The hāʾ is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (أعمالهم) a second direct object. The wāw is of ḥāl; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يظلمون) its khabar; and the clause is accusative as an emphatic ḥāl. (وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ فِي حَياتِكُمُ الدُّنْيا وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِها) The wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb of time attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "it will be said to them, 'You exhausted…', on the day of their being exposed"; the clause (يعرض) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يعرض) is a passive imperfect verb; (الذين) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (على النار) are attached to (يعرض). (أذهبتم) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (طيباتكم) is a direct object; (في حياتكم) are attached to (أذهبتم); and (الدنيا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (الحياة). More discussion of this verse will come in the section on Rhetoric. (فَالْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (اليوم) is an adverb of time attached to (تجزون); (تجزون) is a passive nominative imperfect verb; (عذاب الهون) is a second direct object; (بما) are attached to (تجزون); (ما) is a relative noun, and it may be maṣdariyya; the clause (كنتم) has no grammatical position; the clause (تستكبرون) is the khabar of (كنتم); (في الأرض) are attached to (تستكبرون); and (بغير الحق) is a ḥāl. (وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded; (ما) may be made maṣdariyya or a relative noun, and the maṣdariyya is preferable. (وَاذْكُرْ أَخا عادٍ إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقافِ) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to command that the story of ʿĀd be mentioned to these polytheists so that they take warning from it. (اذكر) is an imperative verb, its agent latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (أخا عاد) is a direct object; (إذ) is an adverb of past time, and it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) of (أخا عاد), because the brother of ʿĀd — Hūd — is bound up with the time of his warning and what happened to him with them. The clause (أنذر قومه) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; and (بالأحقاف) is a ḥāl of (أخا عاد), and not attached to (أنذر) as appears at first glance, i.e. in the state of their being at al-Aḥqāf; as for the complement of (أنذر), it will come later. (وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ) The wāw is parenthetical and the clause is parenthetical; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (خلت النذر) is a verb and its agent; (من بين يديه) is a ḥāl, and (من خلفه) is conjoined to (من بين يديه). (أن) is maṣdariyya, or lightened from the heavy [أنّ] with its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the clause (لا تعبدوا) its khabar; in either case, it together with what it governs is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أنذر). (لا) is prohibitive; (تعبدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (لا); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and the Name of Majesty is the object of (تعبدوا). (إِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ) (إن) and its noun, and the clause (أخاف) is its khabar; (عليكم) are attached to (أخاف); (عذاب يوم) is a direct object, and (عظيم) is a naʿt of (يوم); and the clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for the prohibition. (قالُوا أَجِئْتَنا لِتَأْفِكَنا عَنْ آلِهَتِنا) (قالوا) is a verb and its agent; the hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (جئتنا) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the lām is causal; (تأفكنا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; and (عن آلهتنا) are attached to (تأفكنا). (فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; (ائت) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (نا) is a direct object; (بما) are attached to (ائت); and the clause (تعدنا) is the ṣila. (إن) is conditional; (كنت) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (كنت): (كان) and its noun, and (من الصادقين) is its khabar; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then bring us what you promise us". (قالَ إِنَّمَا الْعِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) (قال) is a past verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "he", i.e. Hūd; (إنما) is the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (العلم) is a mubtadaʾ; (عند الله) is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَأُبَلِّغُكُمْ ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ وَلكِنِّي أَراكُمْ قَوْماً تَجْهَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction, i.e. as for me, my task is only conveying the message, not bringing the punishment, since I am not able to do it; the only One able to do it is Allah the Exalted. (أبلغكم) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "I", and the kāf is a direct object; (ما) is a direct object; the clause (أرسلت) is the ṣila; (أرسلت) is a passive past verb; (به) are attached to (أرسلت). The wāw is a conjunction; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (أراكم) is its khabar; (قوما) is a second direct object, and the clause (تجهلون) is an adjective of (قوما). (فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عارِضاً مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ قالُوا هذا عارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنا) The fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted, implied clause, its implied form being "so they persisted in their insistence and their demand for
the punishment, and it came to them; and when they saw it…". (لما) is temporal ("when") or linking; (رأوه) is a past verb, its agent and its direct object; (عارضا) is a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual; and it was said that it is a tamyīz (specification). (مستقبل أوديتهم) is a naʿt; this is permitted because the annexation is not pure, so it does not make it definite, and it can therefore serve as an adjective of the indefinite noun, i.e. heading and moving towards them. The clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of (لما), which contains the sense of condition in any case. (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ and (عارض) its khabar; (ممطرنا) is a naʿt of (عارض), and the adjective is permitted for the reason given above, i.e. "bringing rain to us". Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj said: the pronoun in (رأوه) refers to something not mentioned, which is made clear by His words (عارضا); so the pronoun refers to the cloud, i.e. when they saw the cloud spreading across. (بَلْ هُوَ مَا اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ رِيحٌ فِيها عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (بل) is a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb) — Hūd said that. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (ما) the khabar; the clause (استعجلتم) is the ṣila, and (به) belongs to the ṣila; (ريح) is a badal (substitute) of (ما), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is a wind"; (فيها) is a fronted khabar, (عذاب) a postponed mubtadaʾ and (أليم) a naʿt; and the clause (فيها عذاب أليم) is a naʿt of (ريح). It was also said that it is part of the speech of Allah the Exalted, but the first is more fitting and more grounded in eloquence. (تُدَمِّرُ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ بِأَمْرِ رَبِّها) The clause is a second naʿt of (ريح); (تدمر) is an imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "it"; (كل شيء) is a direct object; (بأمر) are attached to (تدمر) [Translator's note: printed «بندمر», an evident misprint]; and (ربها) is muḍāf ilayhi. (فَأَصْبَحُوا لا يُرى إِلَّا مَساكِنُهُمْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. Hūd said that, then the wind overtook them, and they became such that nothing was seen but their dwellings. If the saying is from Allah the Exalted, the fāʾ is merely a conjunction. (كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْقَوْمَ الْمُجْرِمِينَ) (كذلك) is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); (نجزي) is an imperfect verb, its agent latent, its implied form being "We"; (القوم) is a direct object, and (المجرمين) a naʿt of (القوم). (وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِيما إِنْ مَكَّنَّاكُمْ فِيهِ) The wāw is the wāw of oath, and the lām is [the lām of] the reply to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (مكناهم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (فيما) are attached to (مكناهم); (ما) is a relative noun in the sense of "that which", or a described [indefinite] noun. On (إن) there are three views. The first: it is conditional, with its apodosis omitted, and the conditional clause is the ṣila of (ما), the implied form being "in that in which, if We had established you in it, you would have transgressed". The second: it is redundant (zāʾida), by likening the relative mā to the negating mā and the temporal mā. The third, and it is the most probable: it is negating, in the sense of mā, i.e. We established them in that in which We have not established you — of strength, expansion and abundance of provision; and the negating mā was avoided in favour of in to escape bringing together two words identical in sound. A fuller exposition of this discussion will come in the section on Benefits. (مكناكم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object, and (فيه) are attached to (مكناكم). (وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ سَمْعاً وَأَبْصاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلا أَبْصارُهُمْ وَلا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ) (جعلنا) is a verb and its agent; (لهم) are attached to (جعلنا), because it means "We created"; (سمعا) is a direct object, and (أبصارا) and (أفئدة) are conjoined to (سمعا). The fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (أغنى) is a past verb; (عنهم) are attached to (أغنى); (سمعهم) is the agent, and (ولا أبصارهم ولا أفئدتهم) are conjoined to (سمعهم); (من) is a redundant preposition, and (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. any of availing. (إِذْ كانُوا يَجْحَدُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) (إذ) is an adverb of past time conveying cause, attached to the meaning of the negation, because what is given a cause is the negation, i.e. the benefit of these senses was denied them because they used to reject. The author of al-Kashshāf pointed to this, saying: «If you say: by what is (إذ كانوا يجحدون) made accusative? I say: by His words, Exalted is He, (فما أغنى). If you say: why does it function as a statement of cause? I say: because what a statement of cause and an adverb convey is the same in your saying "I struck him for his wrongdoing" and "I struck him when he did wrong", since if you struck him at the time of his wrongdoing, you struck him only because of the existence of his wrongdoing in it; except that "idh" and "ḥaythu" have prevailed in this over the other adverbs» — to the point that it has almost become attached to their conventional meanings. The clause (كانوا) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يجحدون) is its khabar; (بآيات الله) are attached to (يجحدون). (وحاق بهم): the wāw is a conjunction; (حاق) is a past verb, indeclinable on fatḥa; (بهم) are attached to (حاق); (ما) is the agent of (حاق); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يستهزئون) is the khabar; and (به) are attached to (يستهزئون).

* Rhetoric:
In His words, Exalted is He, «ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار» to the end of the verse, there is the device of inversion (fann al-qalb), which has been discussed before, according to the view of some, and that the original is "the Fire will be presented to them". On this view, it is said to them before entering it, i.e. on beholding it. Among those who held this view are al-Zamakhsharī and al-Jalāl. The text of al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «Their being exposed to the Fire is their being punished by it, from their saying "the Banū so-and-so were exposed to the sword" when they were killed by it; and from it are His words, Exalted is He: (النار يعرضون عليها). It may also be meant that the Fire is presented to them, from their saying "the she-camel was presented to the watering-trough", meaning the presenting of the trough to her, so they inverted it. The explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, indicates this: they will be brought to it and it will be uncovered for them.» It was said in rebuttal of al-Zamakhsharī that there is nothing compelling inversion [in the camel example] except that [the trough] is inanimate, without perception, while the she-camel is the perceiving one, so she is the one to whom the trough is presented; as for the Fire, texts have come stating that it will then be perceptive with the perception of animals, indeed the perception of those endowed with knowledge, so the matter in the verse is on its apparent meaning. The wording of Zāda in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī: «ʿArḍ is made transitive with lām and with ʿalā; one says "I presented to him (ʿaraḍtu lahu) such-and-such a matter" and "I presented the thing to him (ʿalayhi)", i.e. I showed it to him. He, Exalted is He, said: (وعرضنا جهنم للكافرين عرضا). Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. We brought it out so that the disbelievers looked at it. So the one to whom something is presented must be one possessed of awareness, and the Fire is not one of them; so the presenting must be taken as punishing figuratively, by way of expressing a thing by the name of what leads to it, as one says "the Banū so-and-so were exposed to the sword and were killed by it"; or it remains on its original meaning, and the speech is taken as inversion, the original being "and the day the Fire will be presented to those who disbelieved", i.e. shown and brought out before them. The subtle point in regarding it as inversion is hyperbole, by claiming that the Fire has discernment, domination and mastery.»
As for Shaykh Abū Ḥayyān, he rejected the inversion and said, in the course of rebutting al-Zamakhsharī: «The Quran should not be taken as inversion, since the correct view on inversion is that it is among the things to which one is forced in poetry. If the meaning is sound and clear without inversion, what necessity calls for it? Neither their saying "I presented the she-camel to the trough" nor the explanation of Ibn ʿAbbās contains anything indicating inversion, because presenting the she-camel to the trough and presenting the trough to the she-camel are each sound, since presenting is a relative matter that may be attributed to either the she-camel or the trough.»

* Benefits:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «(إن) is negating, i.e. in that in which We have [not] established you [Translator's note: the printed quotation reads «فيما مكنّاكم فيه», without the negating مَا that the sense requires], except that in is better in sound because of the repugnant repetition involved in mā's being joined with its like, and the like of that is avoided. Do you not see that the origin of mahmā is mā mā, and because of the repugnance of the repetition they changed the alif to hāʾ? Abū al-Ṭayyib was clumsy in his saying:
لعمرك ما ما بان منك لضارب ... بأقتل مما بان منك لغائب
(By your life, what showed from you to one who strikes is not more deadly than what showed from you to one absent.)
What would it have harmed him to imitate the sweetness of the wording of the Revelation and say "laʿamruka mā in bāna minka li-ḍāribin"? And in has been made a connective [redundant particle] just like it in what al-Akhfash recited:
يرجى المرء ما إن لا يراه ... وتعرض دون أذناه الخطوب
(A man hopes for what he will not see, while misfortunes block the way before [even] the nearest of it.)»
This is what al-Zamakhsharī said. The reading in his Dīwān is:
يرى أن ما ما بان منك لضارب ... بأقتل مما بان منك لعائب
(He sees that what showed from you to one who strikes is not more deadly than what showed from you to one who reproaches.)
Ibn Jinnī said: «The first mā is redundant, and the second is in the sense of "that which", and the noun of anna is implied in it.» Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said: «Al-Mutanabbī said: the first mā is in the sense of laysa, and the second in the sense of "that which".» The meaning he intends is that what showed from you to one who strikes is not more deadly than what showed to a reproacher who finds fault with you; he means that reproach is harsher than killing. This is taken from the saying of Ḥabīb ibn Aws, Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī:
فمتى لا يرى أن الفريصة مقتل ... ولكن يرى أن العيوب مقاتل
(A young man who does not see the shoulder-flesh as a mortal spot, but sees that faults are the mortal spots.) [Translator's note: the first word is printed «فمتى»; the gloss follows the evident reading «فتى».]

dervis-irab:27-32.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنا ما حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْقُرى وَصَرَّفْنَا الْآياتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ) Resumptive speech, introduced to address the people of Mecca by way of illustration. The lām is the reply to the omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realisation; (أهلكنا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حولكم) is an adverb attached to an omitted element that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (من القرى) are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (صرفنا) is conjoined to (أهلكنا), and (الآيات) is a direct object; (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (يرجعون) is its khabar (predicate). (فَلَوْلا نَصَرَهُمُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ قُرْباناً آلِهَةً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لولا) is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), equivalent to hallā; (نصرهم) is a past verb and a fronted direct object; (الذين) is a postponed agent; the clause (اتخذوا) is the ṣila; (من دون الله) are attached to (اتخذوا). The first object of (اتخذوا) is omitted, and it is the referent pronoun of the relative noun; (قربانا) is accusative as a ḥāl, and (آلهة) is a second object. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Ḥūfī held that the first object is likewise omitted, as established above, with (قربانا) as the second object and (آلهة) a badal (substitute) of it. Al-Zamakhsharī condemned this view and said that the meaning is corrupted by it, but he did not explain how the meaning is corrupted; we shall explain it, and say: if (قربانا) were the second object, with the meaning "a means of drawing near", the meaning would come to be that they were rebuked for failing to take Allah as a means of drawing near; because when a master rebukes his slave and says "you have taken a master other than me", it means only blame for attributing mastership to someone other than him. That is not the intent here, for Allah the Exalted is the One to whom one draws near, not the One by whom one draws near to another. The rebuke fell only on attributing divinity to other than Allah the Exalted, so the speech properly requires that (آلهة) be the second object and nothing else. Abū Ḥayyān and Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted parsing (قربانا) as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with (آلهة) as the second object and the first object omitted, as above. (بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهُمْ وَذلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction, for moving from the denial of help to something more specific than it, since the denial of help would hold true with their [gods] being present with them without helping; so by the digression He conveyed that they were not present at all, let alone helping them. (ضلوا) is a verb and its agent; (عنهم) are attached to (ضلوا). The wāw is a conjunction; (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (إفكهم) a khabar. (وما): the wāw is a conjunction and (ما) is maṣdariyya or a relative noun, the meaning being "and their fabrication" or "and what they fabricate"; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يفترون) is the khabar of (كان). (وَإِذْ صَرَفْنا إِلَيْكَ نَفَراً مِنَ الْجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقُرْآنَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذ) is an adverb governed by an omitted (اذكر); the clause (صرفنا) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (صرفنا) is a verb and its agent; (إليك) are attached to (صرفنا); (نفرا) is a direct object; (من الجن) is an adjective of (نفر); and the clause (يستمعون القرآن) is a second adjective of (نفرا), or a ḥāl, because it has been specified by the adjective. (فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قالُوا: أَنْصِتُوا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is temporal ("when") or linking; (حضروه) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause (أنصتوا) is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and the pronoun in (حضروه) refers to the Quran. (فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوْا إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ) Conjoined to what preceded; (قضي) is a passive past verb; the clause (ولّوا) has no grammatical position; (إلى قومهم) are attached to (ولّوا); and (منذرين) is a ḥāl. (قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إِنَّا سَمِعْنا كِتاباً أُنْزِلَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ) (قالوا) is a verb and its agent; (إن) and its noun, and the clause (سمعنا) is its khabar; (كتابا) is a direct object; the clause (أنزل) is an adjective of (كتابا), and it is passive, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (من بعد) are attached to (أنزل), and (موسى) is muḍāf ilayhi; (مصدقا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (كتابا); (لما) are attached to (مصدقا); (بين) is an adverb attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (يديه) is muḍāf ilayhi. (يَهْدِي إِلَى الْحَقِّ وَإِلى طَرِيقٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ)
The clause (يهدي) is a second naʿt of (كتابا), or a ḥāl of it because it has been described — the rule has been given before. (إلى الحق) are attached to (يهدي), and (إلى صراط مستقيم) is conjoined to (إلى الحق) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads (وإلى طريق مستقيم)]. (يا قَوْمَنا أَجِيبُوا داعِيَ اللَّهِ وَآمِنُوا بِهِ يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُجِرْكُمْ مِنْ عَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ) (يا) is a vocative particle, and (قومنا) is an annexed munādā (one addressed); (أجيبوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (داعي الله) is a direct object; (آمنوا) is conjoined to (أجيبوا), and (به) are attached to (آمنوا). (يغفر) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the reply to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); (لكم) are attached to (يغفر), and (من ذنوبكم) are also attached to (يغفر), i.e. some of them, so (من) is partitive — the secret of the partitive will come in the section on Rhetoric. (ويجركم من عذاب أليم) is conjoined to what preceded. (وَمَنْ لا يُجِبْ داعِيَ اللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ بِمُعْجِزٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; (من) is conditional, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ;
(لا) is negating; (يجب) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, and (داعي الله) is its object. The fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition, because the apodosis is a non-inflecting (jāmid) verb. (ليس) is a defective past verb; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) particle, and (معجز) is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the khabar of (ليس), whose noun is latent, referring to (من); (في الأرض) are attached to (معجز). (وَلَيْسَ لَهُ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءُ أُولئِكَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; (ليس) is a defective past verb; (له) is the fronted khabar of (ليس); (من دونه) is a ḥāl; (أولياء) is the postponed noun of (ليس). (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (في ضلال) is the khabar of (أولئك), and (مبين) is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم» there is the device of pointed allusion (fann al-tankīt): He expressed it with the partitive (من) to indicate that forgiveness falls on private sins; as for the rights of [Allah's] servants, they cannot be forgiven except after their owners are satisfied, for Allah the Exalted does not forgive, through faith, the sins of wrongs done to others.

dervis-irab:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى) The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is conjoined to an implied clause; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (يروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (أن) and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of (يروا). (أن) and its noun; (الذي) is an adjective of (الله), and the clause (خلق السموات والأرض) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (الذي). The wāw is a conjunction; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; (يعي) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (بخلقهنّ) are attached to (يعي). The bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (قادر) is genitive in form and nominative in position because it is the khabar (predicate) of (أن); the redundant bāʾ entered only because the negation at the beginning of the verse includes أن and what is in its domain. More of this discussion will come in the section on Benefits. (على أن يحيي الموتى) is attached to (قادر). (بَلى إِنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (بلى) is a particle of answer for cancelling a negation: it cancels the negation and affirms its opposite; the discussion of the difference between it and naʿam has been given before. (إن) and its noun, and (قدير) is its khabar; (على كل شيء) are attached to (قدير). (وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ أَلَيْسَ هذا بِالْحَقِّ) The wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "it will be said to them", and the clause is resumptive. The clause (يعرض) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يعرض) is a passive imperfect verb; (الذين) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (على النار) are attached to (يعرض). The clause (أليس هذا بالحق) is the object of the saying that makes the adverb accusative. The hamza is of disapproving, rebuking interrogation; (ليس) is a defective past verb; (هذا) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant preposition; and (الحق) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ليس). (قالُوا بَلى وَرَبِّنا قالَ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ) (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (بلى) is a particle of answer; the wāw is of oath; (ربنا) is genitive by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an implied verb, its implied form being "I swear". (قال) is a past verb; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (ذوقوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; (العذاب) is an object; (بما) are attached to (ذوقوا); the bāʾ is causal and (ما) is maṣdariyya, i.e. because of your disbelief; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تكفرون) is its khabar. (فَاصْبِرْ كَما صَبَرَ أُولُوا الْعَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the end of the disbelievers is as mentioned, then be patient with their harm. (اصبر) is an imperative verb, indeclinable on sukūn, its agent latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; (كما صبر) is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a ḥāl (circumstantial); (أولو العزم) is the agent of (صبر), and (من الرسل) is a ḥāl. (وَلا تَسْتَعْجِلْ لَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ما يُوعَدُونَ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إِلَّا ساعَةً مِنْ نَهارٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تستعجل) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), its agent latent, its implied form being "you"; (لهم) are attached to (تستعجل); and the object of (تستعجل) is omitted, its implied form being "the descent of the punishment". (كأن) and its noun; (يوم) is an adverb attached to the negation conveyed by (لم); the clause (يرون) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يرون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (يوعدون) is the ṣila. The clause (لم يلبثوا) is the khabar of (كأن); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ساعة) is an adverb attached to (يلبثوا); and (من نهار) is an adjective of (ساعة). (بَلاغٌ فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْفاسِقُونَ) (بلاغ) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this with which you have been admonished is a proclamation"; and it was said its implied form is "this Quran". The fāʾ is made a conjunction [Translator's note: the source reads «فجعل الفاء عاطفة», apparently for «والفاء عاطفة», "the fāʾ is a conjunction"]; (هل) is an interrogative particle whose meaning is negation; (يهلك) is a passive imperfect verb; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (القوم) is the deputy agent, and (الفاسقون) an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His words, Exalted is He, «ولم يعي بخلقهن» there is a synecdochic trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is causality, because ʿayy, i.e. fatigue, is impossible for Him, Exalted is He; and it is a cause of ceasing work, or of deficiency in it and delay in completing it — that is the relation in this trope.

* Benefits:
Al-Zajjāj said: «If you said "I did not think that Zayd was standing (bi-qāʾimin)", it would be permissible; it is as though it were said "Is not Allah able (bi-qādirin)?" Do you not see that (بلى) occurs affirming the power over everything — the resurrection and other things — not their seeing?» Abū Ḥayyān said in comment on it: «The correct view is to restrict that to what is heard [from the Arabs] (al-samāʿ).»
Ibn Hishām said: a thing may be given the ruling of what resembles it in meaning, in wording, or in both. As for the first, it has many forms, one of which is the entry of the bāʾ into the khabar of anna in His words, Exalted is He: (أو لم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض ولم يعي بخلقهنّ بقادر), because it is in the sense of "Is not Allah able?"; and what made that implied structure easy is the distance between the two [i.e. anna and its khabar]. For that reason it did not enter in: (أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلق السموات والأرض قادر على أن يخلق مثلهم). Similar is the insertion of the bāʾ in (كفى بالله شهيدا), because of the meaning "be content with Allah as witness" that has entered it, unlike his saying:
قليل منك يكفيني
(A little from you suffices me.)
And in his saying:
سود المحاجر لا يقرأن بالسور
(Black around the eyes, they do not recite the surahs.)
because of the meaning "they do not draw near [to Allah] by reciting the surahs" that has entered it. For this reason al-Suhaylī said: you may not say "your letter reached me, so I read with it (qaraʾtu bihi)" on the pattern of his saying "lā yaqraʾna bi-l-suwar", because it is devoid of the meaning of drawing near.
